requirements.statement: Every follow-up row has a rank class, one of product, host, tooling, paperwork, not-verifiable; a legacy row with no recorded class gets one from its summary prefix ([not-verifiable] to not-verifiable, [flaky-ci] to tooling, [review:<label>] to product, and so on). Must pass.
file-followups files and lists rows in rank order (product, host, tooling, paperwork, not-verifiable) across every ledger it reads, and records each row's class with it. Must pass.
/ship-build's readout lists filed and unfiled follow-ups in that same order with the class shown, so product items are read first. Not marked must pass.

A new library packages/core/lib/followup-rank.js owns the five classes and their order; classOf(row) returns a recorded rankClass when valid, otherwise a class derived from prefix and status; rank(rows) stable-sorts into class order carrying class; its CLI 'open --state-dir <dir> [...]' prints merged, ranked open rows each with class and dir.
discovered.record keeps a valid rankClass field on a new row; no existing producer changes.

file-followups step 3 reads rows through the followup-rank CLI; step 4 files in that order and records { summary, url, class } per filed row; step 5 writes data.issues row lines in that order, each starting with the class; data.unfiled lists summaries in that order.
/ship-build's readout states the order and shows the class on every filed, unfiled and recorded-not-yet-filed follow-up line.
docs/guides/ship-build.md's file-followups row says rows are filed product first.
Prefix precedence: recorded rankClass, then status not_verifiable, then prefix, then kind stale-grounding, then product. Unknown rows rank product.
requirements.source: TRD Intended Change (precedence paragraph) and Decision
